To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lesions of the amygdalocortical pathway disrupt the incremental attentional effects observed in rats with sham lesions.
the attentional processing of conditioned stimuli is enhanced by a change in the predictive value of those stimuli.

rats with a neurotoxin lesion of the central nucleus of the amygdale (CN) in the right hemisphere and a neurotoxin (192Ig) lesion of the substantia innominatum/nucleus basallis (SI/NB) in the left hemisphere show a deficit in the incremental attention to a conditioned stimulus when its predictive value changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying the incremental processing of a CS when that CS's value as a signal is changed.
the effects of bilateral and unilateral lesions of the amygdaloid complex on the attentional processes that are thought to mediate the enhanced processing of CSs.
how the brain processes information about the predictive value of CSs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these data support the hypothesis that the central nucleus of the amygdalae (CN) is the critical site of action of the amygdalar afferents to the nucleus basalis magnocellularis (NBM).

the amygdala, particularly the amygdala CN, plays a critical role in mediating attention to the environment, and the SI/nBM, which is the source of a large cholinergic input to the amygdala and other brain areas, plays a critical modulatory role in this process.
these data support the notion that the amygdala is a critical component of a neural system for processing the predictive value of CSs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amygdala and SI/nBM are necessary for incremental CS processing and that these structures are necessary for this processing when the CS is presented unilaterally.
the CN is necessary for the incremental attentional processes that accompany changes in CS predictive value, and that this effect is mediated by the SI/nBM and its connections.
the SI/nBM, which receives a dense projection from the CN, may play a critical role in the incremental attention to the CSs of a stimulus compound.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the amygdala and basal forebrain are involved in the processing of salient events, but they do not appear to play a role in the incremental processing of a CS when the CS's predictive value is changed.
the amygdala, and in particular the central nucleus, is involved in processing the predictive value of a CS.
the amygdala is a critical brain region for learning and memory.
